answer: Each agent carries a signed, time‑stamped voucher recorded in a distributed ledger we call the Prism. When a new node joins, it must present vouchers from at least three existing agents whose reputations form an Orchard of mutually‑vouched peers; the ledger’s Beacon periodically audits voucher chains, revoking any that reference a node later flagged as Sybil. An attacker therefore must bribe or compromise dozens of already‑trusted agents, inflating the cost to prohibitive levels.
